answerChoices.text: one negative root and one positive root

solutions.text:
The first equation gives \(x=\pm3.\) Factoring the difference of squares in the second gives \[ \begin{aligned} &[(2x-1)-(x-1)]\\ &\quad\cdot[(2x-1)+(x-1)]\\ &\qquad=x(3x-2)=0, \end{aligned} \] so \(x=0\) or \(\frac{2}{3}.\) Squaring the third gives \(x^2-x-6=0,\) with candidates \(3\) and \(-2;\) only \(3\) satisfies the real-domain restrictions. Every root obtained is at most \(3.\)

Thus, each equation has no root greater than \(3,\) and the correct answer is B.
